specs.item: P1-36 — Marathi/Hindi label toggle for SHELL CHROME (www/index.html only)
specs.summary: Add an English (default) / Marathi / Hindi language toggle that swaps SHELL CHROME labels only. Approach = a static `data-i18n` attribute pass (additive attributes on chrome elements) walked by a new `applyLang()`, PLUS a tiny `stT(key)` lookup used at the exact spots in renderHome() where labels are JS-generated (they get overwritten each render, so an attribute alone would be clobbered). New backed-up control pref `saagar_lang` ('en'|'mr'|'hi', default 'en'), added to appControlKeys(), naming already matches APP_RE (saagar_ prefix) and passes restore via the control ok:true fallthrough. A "Language / भाषा" card in Settings (sibling of the existing Display-mode card #uiModeCard) hosts a 3-way segmented control. Missing translations fall back to English (and ultimately to the hand-written English already in the DOM, never clobbered). Scope is strictly shell chrome — NOT module iframes, NOT saagar-report.js content, NOT user data / proper nouns. All grounded in the real file (no existing i18n system: `data-i18n`/`applyLang`/`getLang` grep empty; html lang="en" @L2).

specs.approach: Hybrid, primary = additive `data-i18n` attribute pass; justification vs a pure render-time t() map: (1) Most high-value chrome (bottom nav, 8 config subtabs, Settings-hub header, home section headings, hero footer, modules/reports/today headings, display-mode card) lives in STATIC HTML that is parsed once and never regenerated — tagging it with data-i18n and walking it in applyLang() translates everything in a single pass with ZERO edits to render functions and preserves existing behaviour byte-for-byte (we only ADD attributes / wrap text in spans). A pure t() map would force converting that static HTML into JS-rendered strings = rewriting large spans, which the hard rules forbid. (2) A small, known set of labels is generated by JS inside renderHome() (heroNetLabel, the 5 hero-stat captions, the 6 quick-tile labels, ownerLine, the empty-state) — these get overwritten on every render, so a data-i18n attribute would be clobbered; for exactly these spots we wrap the literal in stT(key) at the assignment. (3) Re-translation triggers: applyLang() runs once in init() and on every setLang() toggle. It does NOT need to run inside renderHome, because (a) no data-i18n element sits inside an innerHTML-replaced host — the re-rendered hosts (#attentionList, #quickGrid, #heroStats, #empStats) contain DATA, while the chrome-label elements are static siblings — and (b) the JS-generated labels already read the live language via stT() at render time. Fallback chain: stT() returns dict[lang][key] ?? en[key] ?? null; applyLang skips null so the original hand-written English in the DOM is the ultimate fallback and is never destroyed. Devanagari (mr/hi) is LTR so no dir/RTL work. No new libraries, no new fonts — Devanagari renders via the existing font stack's OS fallback (system-ui/Roboto→Noto Devanagari on Android), fully offline.

Saved on this device." (itself translated via data-i18n so it localises too). specs.item: P1-38 — Attention Centre with dismiss/snooze (Home attention list in www/index.html)
specs.summary: Add per-item DISMISS and SNOOZE controls to the Home "Needs attention" list, backed by ONE new additive pref key. renderHome() (index.html ~L3152-3278) today builds an unordered items[] array (each {color,em,title,msg,action,cta}) with NO stable id and blindly renders items.slice(0,6) into #attentionList (~L3271-3272), toggling the bell dot #homeBellDot on items.length>0 (~L3275). The fix: (1) derive a STABLE per-item id from a hash of its title (which already embeds area+numbers) via the existing simpleHash() (~L2148); (2) persist dismiss/snooze state in a new key st_v5_attn_state_v1 shaped {dismissed:{id:'YYYY-MM-DD'}, snoozed:{id:'YYYY-MM-DD'}}; (3) filter items before rendering so DISMISS suppresses the current instance only for the rest of TODAY (reappears next calendar day if the condition recurs) and SNOOZE hides until a chosen future date; (4) the bell dot reflects only the post-filter ACTIVE count; (5) upgrade the already-wired bell handler openAttention() (~L3344, the ONLY caller is the bell at ~L1160) into an "Attention Centre" modal that lists ALL active items (not just 6) with controls plus a "Snoozed & dismissed" section with a Restore/un-snooze button. Fully additive: when the key is absent, attnLoadState() returns empty and the rendered list is byte-identical to today.

specs.approach: Stable identity via title-hash (lowest blast radius): items already embed area+emoji+numbers in title, so attnId(it)=simpleHash(title) yields distinct ids per distinct message WITHOUT editing the ~12 inline push() sites — the id is computed centrally in one loop just before rendering. Recurrence is achieved by DATE-SCOPING the dismiss: dismiss stores todayIso() and only suppresses while that equals the current day, so a recurring condition (same title next day, e.g. a 'Stock: not locked' exception re-emitted by the bridge) produces the same id but the stale dismissed date no longer matches → it resurfaces. Snooze stores a future date and suppresses until then; un-snooze/restore lives in the modal. GC in attnLoadState() prunes inert dismissed (date!=today) and expired snoozed (date<=today) entries so the blob never grows. Everything is additive and gated on the key's presence.

Copy: dismiss tooltip 'Dismiss for today — returns tomorrow if still open'; snooze tooltip 'Snooze — hide for a few days'. The bell (🔔 #homeBell) now opens the Attention Centre modal (title 'Needs attention') with two sections: 'Active (N)' listing ALL active items (no 6-cap) each with CTA + a snooze choice (1 day / 3 days / 1 week) + Dismiss; and 'Snoozed & dismissed' listing suppressed items muted (.attn.snoozed) with a 'Restore' button and the return date. specs.item: P1-39 — Text-size setting (Normal / Large) for shell chrome (index.html)
specs.summary: Add a device-local "Text size" preference (Normal default / Large) that applies a modest proportional zoom to the shell CHROME CONTENT scroller only, leaving the fixed topbar/bottom-nav and the module iframe untouched. The feature is a byte-for-byte clone of the EXISTING "Display mode" (saagar_ui_mode) pref pattern: a segmented control in the Config page, a new per-device localStorage key, an apply-on-boot call, and a class toggled on <html>. Mechanism: a class `st-textsize-large` on `document.documentElement` drives a single CSS rule `html.st-textsize-large #mainContent{ zoom:1.12 }`. Because #mainContent (.main, the `overflow:hidden auto` chrome scroller at index.html L131/L1150) is a SEPARATE element from the topbar, the .botnav, and the module overlay (#moduleScreen, a position:fixed sibling at L592/L1630 that hosts #moduleFrame), scaling #mainContent enlarges every chrome view (home/today/modules/reports/config) WITHOUT scaling nav chrome or module content — so it is inherently chrome-only with no iframe-injection changes. `zoom` (not font-size) is chosen because the design is px-based (body 14px + hundreds of explicit `font-size:Npx` rules that do not inherit), so root/body font-size scaling would barely move; zoom scales text AND its container together, which is the LEAST likely to clip. Key registration mirrors saagar_ui_mode exactly (see collisionNotes / newKeysOrFields).

Do NOT scale <html>/<body>/.app — .app is position:fixed;inset:0 (L68) and zooming the root would recompute the fixed full-screen grid against a zoomed viewport and can push .botnav off-screen. Scope strictly to #mainContent. Reuse — no other CSS edits.

newKeysOrFields.storageRulesNote: Mirrors saagar_ui_mode EXACTLY. (a) NOT added to appControlKeys() ⇒ excluded from manual backup/migration export (appStorage filters on isWhitelistedAppKey) — intended, since text size is per-device. (b) Matches APP_RE (`saagar_` prefix at L5684) ⇒ wiped by factory reset AND included in the pre-reset safety backup (factoryResetSafetyBackup iterates APP_RE-matched keys, L5715). (c) Restore: not whitelisted ⇒ validateRestoreData rejects it (never imported from another device); it is NOT in restoreBlockedKeys, and no validateRestoreKeyValue control-branch entry is needed. Net: same lifecycle as the display-mode pref.

specs.approach: Additive clone of the existing Display-mode (setUiMode/saagar_ui_mode) machinery — the safest possible path because it copies a shipped, verified pattern. 1) MECHANISM: a class `st-textsize-large` on document.documentElement (mirrors the existing `bcc-mobile` class convention) gates one CSS rule that applies `zoom:1.12` to `#mainContent` only. #mainContent (.main) is the chrome content scroller (`overflow:hidden auto`, L131-135) holding all five chrome views (homeView/todayView/modulesView/reportsView/configView, L1155-1287). The topbar (.topbar) and bottom nav (.botnav) are grid siblings OUTSIDE .main, and the module iframe lives in #moduleScreen — a position:fixed;inset:0 sibling overlay (L592/L1630) — so zooming #mainContent scales chrome content while leaving nav chrome and module content pixel-identical. 2) WHY zoom, not font-size/root: the design is px-based (body 14px at L57; the vast majority of chrome text sets its own explicit `font-size:Npx` — e.g. .card p 13px, .attn-text 11-13px, .btn 13px — none of which inherit a root/body change), so a root or body font-size bump would be nearly invisible, whereas `zoom` proportionally scales text + padding + container together (less clipping than font-only, which would overflow fixed-width pills/badges). WebView target is Chromium (Android System WebView + desktop Chromium per the desktop-layout-fix history) where `zoom` is supported. 3) PERSISTENCE: reflectTextSizeUI() is called once in init() right after reflectUiModeUI() (L7108), reading the saved key synchronously before first render. 4) CHROME-ONLY (no iframe propagation) is the deliberate recommendation — see 'ui'/'risks' for justification.
specs.ui: Placement: a new 'Text size' card in the Config page, inserted immediately after the existing 'Display mode' card (#uiModeCard, L1292-1299) and before the subtabs nav (L1300) — co-locating the two device-preference toggles. It reuses the identical card + segmented-control markup/styles. Copy: heading '🔎 Text size'; body 'Make on-screen text larger for easier reading. Saved on this device.' (echoes the Display-mode card's 'Saved on this device' wording). Two segmented buttons: 'A Normal' (data-textsize=normal) and 'A Large' (data-textsize=large, with the sample 'A' bumped to font-size:1.15em as a visual cue). The active button is highlighted via the existing `.seg-btn.active` style (navy fill, L792), toggled by reflectTextSizeUI(). On tap, setTextSize() saves, re-applies, and shows a toast ('🔎 Large text' / 'Normal text'). Because the card itself lives inside #mainContent, choosing Large visibly enlarges the settings page including the toggle — expected, immediate feedback (like an OS accessibility control). No topbar icon-button is added (Display mode has one via #uiModeBtn, but text size is a set-and-forget preference; keeping it Config-only avoids topbar crowding — the topbar is already tight at phone widths per the L108-117 audit note).
edgeCases: Fixed-height hero/nav: the topbar and .botnav are OUTSIDE #mainContent (grid siblings) so they are NEVER zoomed — no clipping there. The home hero (.brief/.hero) is INSIDE #homeView (inside #mainContent) so it scales proportionally; since .main scrolls vertically (`overflow:hidden auto`) the taller hero simply scrolls, no clip.

Horizontal clip risk: .main is `overflow:hidden auto` (x hidden). zoom effectively narrows the CSS viewport by the factor, so wide rows/tables could clip horizontally. Mitigation: keep Large modest at 1.12 (not 1.2), and note that data tables already wrap in `.table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}` (L575/L5200) so they self-scroll. Verify the config subtabs nav (L1300, 8 tabs incl. long 'Roles & access') doesn't clip.

Very long labels: zoom scales the label AND its container together, so wrapping/ellipsis behaviour is preserved proportionally (unlike font-only scaling). The one nowrap+ellipsis label (.brand-meta h1, L94) is in the topbar → not zoomed → unaffected.

Two-column wide-screen home: `body[data-view="home"] .main` becomes a grid (L1037-1044) rendering #todayView as a 2nd column above ~768px. At zoom 1.12 the effective CSS width shrinks ~11%; on a small desktop window near the breakpoint the layout could drop to one column earlier. Acceptable (it just stacks) — verify it degrades gracefully.
Module content: opening a module shows #moduleScreen (separate fixed overlay) — text size does NOT apply there by design; module keeps its own sizing + the mobile/desktop display-mode signal.

Modal / toast / FAB text: #modalBackdrop (L1679), #toast (L1690), #st-v5-home-fab/#st-v5-next-chips (L6388-6389) are all body-level position:fixed siblings, NOT inside #mainContent, so their text is NOT scaled in v1. Acceptable limitation (transient surfaces); flagged as open question #2.

Storage unavailable (private mode / quota full): getTextSize() try/catches to 'normal'; setTextSize()'s safeSet may fail silently (safeSet already toasts on quota, L2117) — the class still applies for the session, just not persisted. Same resilience as setUiMode.
Composability with mobile/desktop display mode: text-size class and the `bcc-mobile` class are independent; zoom composes cleanly with either layout. Verify both Mobile and Desktop modes at Large.

Boot ordering: reflectTextSizeUI() runs in init() before doFirstRender/switchView('home'); the #textSizeSeg active class is set as soon as the (always-present, static) config markup exists — no render dependency.
verifySteps: Load the shell in the browser harness (open www/index.html); confirm 0 new console errors on boot.

Config → set Text size = Large; confirm home cards, attention list, config forms, and reports text all grow ~12% while the topbar brand + bottom-nav labels stay unchanged (proves chrome-content-only scoping).
Reload the page; confirm Large persists (apply-on-boot) and the 'Large' seg button shows the active (navy) state.
Open a module (e.g. DSR/QMS) at Large; confirm the module iframe content is pixel-unchanged (proves #moduleScreen is unaffected).

Home at Large: scroll through the hero + all attention cards + module tiles; confirm no horizontal clipping and no content cut off (watch .main overflow-x:hidden). Repeat on a narrow (~360px) viewport.
Config subtabs nav at Large: confirm the 8 tab buttons (incl. 'Roles & access', 'Diagnostics') don't clip/overlap; tables inside Employees/Backup scroll horizontally rather than clip.
Toggle Mobile and Desktop display mode while Large is on; confirm both layouts render correctly (zoom composes with bcc-mobile and the wide-screen two-column home).
Set back to Normal; confirm zoom fully resets (class removed, layout byte-identical to pre-feature).

localStorage check: confirm key `saagar_text_size` = 'large'; run a manual backup export and confirm the key is ABSENT from payload.localStorage (per-device, not exported) — matches saagar_ui_mode behaviour.
Factory-reset dry check (or code-trace): confirm saagar_text_size matches APP_RE and would be both wiped and captured in the pre-reset safety backup.

Regression: with the feature added but Text size = Normal, confirm the whole shell is visually identical to the pristine build (diff against _v6_tools/wave13_pristine/index.pristine.html for the untouched regions).
risks: `zoom` is a non-standard (Chromium) property. It is safe for THIS app (Android System WebView + desktop Chromium), but if the team wants standards-only CSS, the fallback is font-size scaling of .main, which covers far less of this px-based design (only inheriting text). Recommend confirming zoom is acceptable (open question #3).

zoom effectively narrows the CSS viewport; combined with .main's overflow-x:hidden this is the main clipping vector. Mitigated by keeping Large at 1.12 and by pre-existing inner overflow-x:auto on tables — but MUST be verified on narrow widths and the config subtabs.

Scope creep temptation: propagating the scale into module iframes (11 separate base64-embedded documents with dense report/table layouts NOT designed to scale) is high blast-radius and hard to verify. Recommendation: DO NOT propagate in v1 (chrome-only); any future propagation is additive via a new postMessage type (like the dormant ST_SET_DATE at L7057) with per-module opt-in.

Modal/toast/FAB text not scaling could read as inconsistent to a user who set Large. Low severity (transient surfaces); can be extended later by adding those body-level containers to the scale rule if the owner wants it (open question #2).

If a future edit ever moves a position:fixed element to be a DESCENDANT of #mainContent, zoom would misplace it. Currently verified safe: all fixed FABs/chips/toasts/modal are body/.app-level (L6388-6389, L1679-1690), NOT inside .main.

Deviation from the stated hard rule (a) 'add every new key to appControlKeys': intentional and matches the saagar_ui_mode precedent, but needs explicit synthesis-owner sign-off so it isn't flagged as a rule violation (open question #1).

specs.summary: Add ONE new native-vector report `lostWalkinCallSheet` (scope: monthly) to the report engine. specs.approach: ADDITIVE, single-file (saagar-report.js). (a) Decision — NEW report TYPE, not a weekly filter over existing reports. Justification grounded in the code: reports are keyed by `type` in META/BUILDERS and `scope` is pure metadata used only for hub grouping/pack bucketing (list() L1680, row() scope pill L1708, _packTypes L1592) — there is no mechanism to pass a granularity into an existing builder. Most daily builders read single-day localStorage snapshots that do not naturally aggregate (cashDetail per date, DSR per date L261, stockDetailStore per date), so a 'weekly filter over existing' would mean rewriting many builders — a direct violation of the highest-blast-radius 'targeted change / preserve byte-for-byte' rule. QMS is the ONE cross-day-aggregatable source (computeQmsDay(dateIso), already summed across days by monthQms L88-93). So a single new weeklyBrief builder that aggregates the QMS funnel is the minimal, self-contained addition; it mirrors the existing ownerMonthly (L932) / ownerBrief (L99) patterns. (b) Week window — Monday–Sunday ISO week CONTAINING the hub-selected date (opts.date). Justified over rolling-last-7: the hub period control is a single date picker (rptDate) stepping by day (hubStep L1750); anchoring to the calendar week means every day the user steps to within a week yields the SAME stable report and a well-defined 'previous week', which is how owners reason ('this week vs last week'). (c) Comparison — fair same-span: compute nDays = number of week days up to min(weekEnd, today); current window = first nDays of this week, previous window = first nDays of last week (previous Monday +0..nDays-1). A completed past week degrades to full-7-vs-full-7; the in-progress current week compares week-to-date against the same point last week (proper pacing) instead of a misleading partial-vs-full. deltaOf() is null-safe when last week is zero. (d) Hub — new 'Weekly · Owner' GROUP + TAGS entry + the scope-pill ternary extended to 'Weekly'. (e) pack('weekly') — spec'd but recommended deferred (single report). Everything else (list, history, filename which uses opts.date, forModule) works unchanged.
